sam.devex: :wave: Hi all — I'm starting this week and hitting a blocker with secrets. Trying to get a DB password for a personal dev stack and not sure which path or request flow to use. 

lee.security: welcome! :lock: For onboarding/dev secrets we prefer short-lived creds where possible. If it's a personal dev DB, request a dev secret via the Secrets Request form (https://redwood.internal/tools/secrets-request). Include repo, env (dev/staging), and justification.

sam.devex: thanks — is there a CLI flow or only the form?

lee.security: there are two flows:
1) Quick dev tokens via the form (auto-provisioned, TTL 24h by default).
2) For service or long-lived secrets, open a ticket in #eng-infra with the template. Team will provision a Vault path and KMS encryption.

rohit.eng: if you need to read a secret locally, use the dev-k8s service account or our vault CLI. Example: 
```
vault kv get secret/data/dev/sam_myservice
```
Make sure your IAM role is added to the allowed_principals on the path.

sam.devex: do we have naming conventions? I don't want to accidentally put prod creds in dev.

lee.security: yes — use prefixes: `secret/data/dev/<team>-<service>` for dev, `secret/data/stage/...`, `secret/data/prod/...`. Never store plaintext in repos. We also tag paths with `owner` and `rotation_policy`.

jen.devops: small note — Redwood uses AWS KMS to envelope-encrypt Vault's storage keys. For private deployments customers may use their own KMS/HSM. If you need to request a KMS key, mention cloud account and region in the ticket.

sam.devex: who approves rotation requests? I need to rotate a service token my script uses.

lee.security: rotation ownership is: 
- application-owned secrets: app team triggers rotation (we can grant rotate permissions). 
- platform-managed service credentials: platform ops rotates on schedule (default 90d) or immediately on incident.
If you need a rotation, add `rotation: urgent` to the ticket and @jen.devops will pick it up.

rohit.eng: if you want to automate rotations, we have a small library `redwood-secrets` that hits the Vault API and commits new creds to the CI secret store. Link: https://git.redwood/internal/redwood-secrets (readme has examples).

sam.devex: is there any policy about printing secrets in logs?

lee.security: never log secrets. We run scans for common leak patterns in CI and will create alerts. If you find something, DM me or open a #security incident.

deploy-bot: [deploy] env:dev/my-service - secret read attempt by sam.devex at 1711306000: access granted (ttl 23h59m).

sam.devex: got it. I filled the secrets form and linked the repo. I put dev path `secret/data/dev/sam-personal-db`. Is that ok?

lee.security: looks fine, I'll approve the form now. I'll also add your dev role to that path for 7 days so you can test. :thumbsup:

secbot: Reminder: rotation policy applied to `secret/data/dev/sam-personal-db` = 30d (dev default). To request non-default TTL/rotation attach justification to the ticket.

sam.devex: perfect — thanks everyone! One last Q, who do I ping if the CLI token doesn't refresh?

jen.devops: ping #eng-infra and mention me (@jen.devops). If it's CI-related, also tag @rohit.eng.

sam.devex: thank you — closing this thread once I verify access. :slightly_smiling_face:
